text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 0.92% today to close at $473.69, paring back most of a strong two-week rally. The modest decline comes as oil prices have pulled back slightly—U.S. crude sits at $101.91 per barrel, down from the $110+ levels that drove the stock up 9% over the past two weeks on geopolitical supply fears from Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and Iranian escalation around the Strait of Hormuz. Refineries are running at a healthy 93.5% utilization with crude inventories at 698 million barrels, so there's no structural demand problem; today's move appears to reflect a brief cooling of the geopolitical premium rather than any fundamental shift.

The broader context is that refiner stocks like Marathon tend to benefit when crude prices spike on supply concerns—those higher oil costs can be passed along through fuel sales—but they're sensitive to every shift in that risk premium. With Saudi Arabia postponing its investor conference and Houthis continuing attacks, the supply threat remains real, which is likely why the stock held onto most of its two-week gains despite today's small pullback.
